### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**15** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class), packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class), packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_

- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class), MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class), packageId (literal, a string literal in stampedForSlot))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `777e85ddb52eae0534bdbee29438facc1c856a6c` — the merge of head `ed9e3a95e2f5ba85cc9a17f16e725bbc0b547b1a` into base `e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 777e85ddb52eae0534bdbee29438facc1c856a6c && git checkout 777e85ddb52eae0534bdbee29438facc1c856a6c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 ed9e3a95e2f5ba85cc9a17f16e725bbc0b547b1a && git checkout -B drift-repro e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 && git merge --no-ff ed9e3a95e2f5ba85cc9a17f16e725bbc0b547b1a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3300a61212c6dbbb5c92499df5ab1806126c35e3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-history.object.ts, .changeset/32717-rollback-door-one-answer.md + packages/metadata/src/metadata-history.test.ts

This reviews the mechanics only. The platform rule (`/meta` rollback answering the other way) is with seat 5 and is not judged here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The two narrowing arms are right.**
  - *Addressed rollback to an unattributed version on one slot.* `rollbackSlot` reads the history row (`historyVersionRow`) and takes its attribution whenever the row exists. A row attributed to none therefore stays `undefined`. Addressed, it answers `historyVersionNotFound` (the manager's own words). With several slots it gets `refuseSeveralSlots` first.
  - *M1: the environment's version addressing the package that took over the one slot.* This now answers "not found". Addressing the environment there is already refused by `refuseSlotNotHeld`, because the environment holds no row.
  - Both run before any write.
  - With several slots, the body stamp no longer wins over an unattributed row, so a B-stamped body can no longer land in B's row (the ⛔ case). The 4 pins plus the ablations measure all of this.
- **must-fix M1: the widening writes a body whose package stamp names a non-holder, and on the environment's row that changes whose row it is.**
  - *The path.* Naming no package, an unattributed version, one slot, and a restored body stamped `_packageId: B` for a package that holds no row: before this PR it was refused 409 `not-held-by-qualifier`. Now it lands, and `registerRollback` writes `metadata: JSON.stringify(restoredData)` with B's stamp kept. Nothing strips or re-stamps it, and `rowToData` serves it as stored.
  - *When the one slot is the environment's row* (`package_id` NULL or `sys_metadata`): `storedRowPackageId` skips the column and reads the body's stamp. After the write, `rowSlots` keys that row as **B's slot**. The environment loses its row, package B gains a name it never declared, and every later read, save, history and rollback treats the row as B's. That is the attribution-by-body this PR set out to remove, now made durable in `sys_metadata`.
  - *When the one slot is a package's* (the PR's pin, slot A): the column keeps the row A's. But the served item carries `_packageId: B`, and readers that take the holder from the listed item's stamp (for example plugin-webhooks' `listedHolderOf`) see B.
  - *The fix.* The simplest fix is to keep the old refusal: a restored body whose `_packageId` names a package other than the slot's (or names one when the slot is the environment's) is refused before any write. This drops the widening, and the arm becomes a pure narrowing. Alternatively, strip or re-stamp the body to the slot's package before the write, keep the widening, and pin the environment-slot case. Either way, add a pin with the **environment's** row as the one slot and assert `rowSlots` / `storedRowPackageId` of the written row afterwards.
- **nit N1 (pre-existing, not this PR).** A history row attributed to A, slot A, and a body stamped B lands B's stamp in A's row, both before and after this PR. If you take the "refuse a stamp that is not the slot's" fix, one guard covers this case too. Otherwise, a follow-up.
- **The metadata-core doc change** ("NULL means not attributed, never the environment") matches `historyRowAttribution` and the `sys_metadata` mark. It is doc-only.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` and `@objectstack/metadata-core: patch` are right for a non-protocol change. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with `!`, BREAKING and one `adr-0087` marker is correct for the two narrowing arms. If M1 is fixed by dropping the widening, delete the "Widened:" sentence and the matching FROM/TO text. If it is fixed by re-stamping, keep the sentence and say the stamp is replaced.

### ③ Boundary flags

- First-party reach: `MetadataManager.rollback` reads the addressed history first, so it answered these cases already. The narrowings reach only a direct caller of `DatabaseLoader.registerRollback`. The M1 path also reaches only a direct caller handing in a body whose stamp disagrees with the version's snapshot.
- Seat 5 has the platform rule. Landing waits for that ruling and for this M1.
- CI at this head: 36 success, 18 skipped, 1 in progress. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head, including the dogfood battery this narrowing arm owes.

### ④ Design judgment

"A history row that exists says whose version it is, and the caller's body never does" is the right rule, and the narrowings follow from it. The same rule implies that the caller's body must not carry a stamp into the stored row either. M1 is the half of that rule this PR does not yet apply.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ed9e3a95e2f5ba85cc9a17f16e725bbc0b547b1a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-history.object.ts, .changeset/32717-rollback-door-one-answer.md + packages/metadata/src/metadata-history.test.ts

This reviews the delta on my FAIL at `3300a61212c6dbbb5c92499df5ab1806126c35e3`. It is read as the three PR commits on top of the main merge `a8c08609` (`cfd4f28b` red pins, `beeac9cc` fix, `ed9e3a95` changeset), so `git diff a8c08609 ed9e3a95`. The rest of the range is main. The platform rule is seat ruling 6885958183 (amended B), and it is applied here, not re-judged.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 closed.** `registerRollback` now writes `stampedForSlot(restoredData, slot.packageId)`.
  - **What gets rewritten.** A package stamp naming another package than the slot's is replaced by the slot's package. On the environment's package-less row the stamp is removed. That covers the envelope's `packageId` and the body's `_packageId`, which are exactly the two stamps `storedItemPackageId` reads, in both the wrapped and the flat shape.
  - **What does not.** A body naming no package, the sentinel, or the slot's own package is returned as the same object, so an agreeing snapshot is restored byte for byte.
  - **What is derived from the written body.** The checksum, the bundle member, the `scope` and the history snapshot are all computed from `written`.
  - **The pin I asked for.** It uses the environment's row as the one slot. It restores versions 1 (unattributed) and 2 (environment's own) with a B-stamped body, both bare and addressing `null`. It asserts that the row stays `package_id NULL` and unstamped, that `load` serves no `_packageId`, and that B is still refused `not-held-by-qualifier` naming only the environment. So the row is still the environment's slot.
- **N1 closed.** Two pins (loader and manager door) restore an A-attributed version with a B-stamped snapshot into A's row. They assert it is written and filed stamped A, and that B's row is byte-identical. The manager files the body the loader returned (`written !== handed`), so the registry and the stored row agree.
- **Ruling B applied.** `isAddressedVersion(row, packageId, sole)`: when the addressed slot is the name's one row slot (`isSoleRowSlot`), a version attributed to none and the environment's own are that slot's. `queryHistory`, `getHistoryRecord` and so `getHistory`/`diff`/`rollback` all read through it, so an addressed read lists exactly what an addressed rollback restores. `rollbackSlot` drops the two "not found" throws and lands those versions addressed or bare. With several slots, an unattributed version is in no addressed history and its rollback is refused `409 ambiguous-in-environment`. The 8 pins × 12 types and the ablations A0–A5 measure each arm.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` and `@objectstack/metadata-core: patch`, `fix(metadata)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. That is correct for a non-protocol change.
- The one narrowing left is declared: an addressed direct `registerRollback`, on a name with several slots, of an unattributed version with a stamped body now answers 409.
- The widening (sole-slot versions at the manager's addressed doors) is in prose.
- BREAKING names who is affected and the fix.
- The adr-0087 marker reason ("the package stamp of the body a rollback writes from now on" moves; no row is rewritten) holds.
- The re-stamp changes what a rollback stores, not what it accepts, so it is no Clause-② arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The area's two carried notes are acknowledged as follow-ups and do not block this PR: an addressed `/meta` rollback on a multi-slot name may answer 404 rather than 409 (area E1), and a departed package's addressed history is still listed (pre-existing).
- CI at this head: 37 success, 18 skipped, none failing. The area reports the dogfood battery green. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

"The history row says whose version it is, and the slot says whose row it is" is now applied at both ends: the body the caller hands in neither attributes the version nor stamps the row. Returning the written body to the manager keeps the served item and the stored row in agreement. The design holds.
